models_evaluated: Respiratory digital twin (LSTM with PhysioMech and PhysioGas modules)

links.outcome: Performance retention on external validation cohorts and multi-step rolling forecasts
links.effect: Model maintained robust performance across external validation cohorts (multi-center eICU and MIMIC-IV); PaO2 MAE 14.15 mmHg overall, ARDS AUROC 0.968. No cohort-level numbers reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Notably, the framework exhibited zero violations of causal consistency tests and maintained robust performance across external validation cohorts and multi-step rolling forecasts.

unlisted_practices: Physics-consistency loss and monotonicity constraints to keep model behavior clinically plausible
Causal consistency testing of what-if ventilator setting simulations

screen.reason: The study develops and retrospectively evaluates a physiological digital twin model (LSTM combined with physics-informed modules) for what-if simulation of ventilator settings on eICU and MIMIC-IV data, without testing an organizational deployment safeguard or human clinical workflow.
